criticalVMs.description: Which VMs are critical. No VM is critical by default.

enabled.description: false turns the plugin off: its topics are removed, and the web UI drops its rail entry, palette entries, overview tiles and panels and shows a switched-off page at its address. Unset turns it on when it has the settings it needs (rustfs is off unless enabled: true, because nothing in its settings says an object store exists); a plugin without them is disabled ("not configured: set plugins.<id>.url", naming the setting to make) and the web UI hides its pages. true with settings missing or invalid makes it unconfigured, which hides its pages too. This is how prometheus, alertmanager, gatus, victorialogs, proxmox, hardware, ssh, kubernetes, flux, cnpg, rustfs, grafana, headlamp and launcher behave, and a change to any of their settings applies live: that plugin restarts, and so do the plugins that use or require it (a prometheus change restarts proxmox, hardware, kubernetes, cnpg and rustfs; a gatus change restarts hardware and kubernetes; a proxmox change restarts hardware; a kubernetes change restarts proxmox, flux and cnpg; a grafana change restarts alertmanager).

node.description: The Proxmox node of the hardware host without a nodename (plugins.hardware.hosts): that host reads the node's series and shows its Proxmox facts, shell link and place in the topology. Hosts with a nodename that is a node of the cluster are that node whatever this says. Empty takes the only node of a one-node cluster; a cluster of several nodes needs it for a host without a nodename. dash reads every node of the cluster either way.

series.description: How the VM chart queries select a VM.

storage.description: Where the Proxmox storage list comes from.

tls.description: How dash verifies the Proxmox API's certificate.

tokenID.description: API token ID, user@realm!tokenname. Proxmox runs only with url, tokenID and tokenSecret all set and is disabled with none of the token set. A token ID without tokenSecret, a tokenSecret without tokenID, or a token without url is a configuration error that stops dash at startup.

tokenSecret.description: API token secret: a literal, env:NAME, file:/path or k8s:<namespace>/<name>#<key> (read from that Kubernetes Secret by the kubernetes plugin, which must run and be allowed to read it). Set together with tokenID: one without the other is a configuration error.

type.description: The plugin type. dash runs one instance per type, so this is empty or the section name.

url.description: Base URL of the Proxmox API, e.g. https://pve.example.com:8006. Required with a token; a URL alone leaves Proxmox disabled.

ids.description: VM ids that are critical. A stopped critical VM is a critical attention item; any other stopped VM is a warning. A JSON list of integers in the environment.

tags.description: VM tags that make a VM critical (compared without regard to case). A JSON list in the environment.

vmSelector.description: The label matcher that selects one VM in the pve-exporter series of the VM charts: one label, = or =~, and a quoted value with {vmid} once, e.g. id="qemu/{vmid}".

source.description: Where the storage list comes from: api reads every node's storages from the Proxmox API (the API token needs the Datastore.Audit privilege); prometheus reads the pve-exporter series pve_disk_usage_bytes, pve_disk_size_bytes, pve_storage_info and pve_storage_shared through the prometheus plugin. A shared storage is listed and counted once, except with prometheus and an exporter without pve_storage_shared, which lists it once per node.

caFile.description: Path of a PEM file with the certificate authority that signed the service's certificate, added to the system roots. Empty uses the system roots only.

insecureSkipVerify.description: Skip verifying the service's certificate and host name. Anyone on the network path can then impersonate the service: prefer caFile.
